paragraphs: InTime sells scheduling software for public safety agencies, built for police, sheriff departments, fire, corrections, and dispatch. The company says it has helped over 500 public safety agencies manage daily scheduling and operations for over 25 years. The head office is in Vancouver, BC.

Beyond shift coverage, the software handles agency leave requests, timebank management, approvals and vacation scheduling. A court and subpoena module adds court appearances to officer schedules, serves electronic subpoenas and communicates with witnesses. Asset tracking assigns vehicles, radios, laptops and firearms to qualified and trained officers.

Anaheim Police Department began using InTime in 2006, replacing spreadsheets for patrol scheduling. That department reports patrol scheduling time falling from about eight hours per cycle to fifteen minutes. Customer data is hosted by Amazon Web Services.

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

paragraphs: Anonymous Alerts sells a reporting platform that gives students, staff and community members a way to raise concerns before they turn into serious incidents. It is used by K-12 schools, districts, colleges and public safety organizations nationwide.

Students can anonymously report bullying, behavioral concerns, threats of violence or mental health risks through a mobile or web interface designed for use across age groups. Designated school administrators receive the information immediately. From a centralized dashboard they can review, manage and investigate reports. Staff can hold real-time conversations with tip submitters while the submitter keeps anonymity. Reporting categories, workflows, notification settings and response protocols can be configured for each organization. A companion panic escalation app lets staff instantly alert administrators and safety personnel.

The company says the system helps schools comply with state laws requiring anonymous reporting systems for school safety and violence prevention. A dedicated page covers Alyssas Law compliance in New York. Newtown Public School District is named on the site as one district that chose the reporting app. The company lists United States patents on the technology, with additional US and non-US patents pending. Anonymous 2-way Communications is registered with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

paragraphs: Automotus sells automated curb management systems to cities and airports. The company says it works with cities, airports and fleets to make communities better places to live.

The cameras attach to existing infrastructure such as streetlight poles. Once installed, the system automates data collection, invoicing and enforcement. Commercial drivers pay for curb time without apps or meters, and agencies can optionally apply discounted rates for electric vehicles. Violations are captured as they occur, with the option of notifying enforcement or issuing a citation automatically. paragraphs: Averhealth provides substance use monitoring and treatment solutions. Its work is built around the needs of criminal justice-based substance use monitoring programs.
